name: Pictory
tagline: Turns scripts and articles into videos with stock visuals, music and AI voice-overs.
best_for: Creating short explainer or social videos from existing text
description:
Pictory is an online video tool that converts written content, such as a script or a blog article, into a finished video. It matches sentences to clips from a licensed library of visuals, adds music and can narrate the text with an AI voice-over.

It suits marketers, educators and bloggers who already have written material and want a quick video version without editing footage by hand. You can adjust scenes, swap visuals and edit captions in the browser after the first draft is generated. A free trial has been offered with a limited number of projects, and paid plans are billed by tier. Plans, limits and features change, so check the official site for current plans.
use_steps: Create an account and start a project from a script or article link.
Review the scenes the tool generates from your text.
Swap visuals, edit captions and choose music and a voice.
Render the video and download or share it.
pros: Starts from text you already have
Captions and voice-over in one place
cons: Free trial is limited to a few projects
use_cases: Turning a blog post into a short video
Making social clips from a script
pricing_details: Pictory has offered a free trial of a few projects, followed by paid plans billed monthly or annually in tiers such as Starter, Professional and Teams. Prices and limits change, so check the official website for current plans.

faq.a: Pictory is an online tool that turns scripts or articles into videos using stock visuals, music and AI voice-overs.
Pictory has offered a free trial with a limited number of projects, with paid plans after that. Confirm current terms on the official site.

faq.q: How should I check results from Pictory?
faq.a: Treat outputs as a first draft. Review the video, voice and on-screen text yourself, confirm you have the rights to any uploaded material, and check licensing and privacy terms on the official website.

name: Fliki
tagline: Text-to-video and AI voice tool for narrated videos from scripts and blog posts.
best_for: Narrated videos with realistic AI voices in many languages
description:
Fliki generates videos from text, scripts and blog posts, pairing visuals with AI voice-overs and subtitles. Its library includes a large set of AI voices across many languages, with voice cloning, plus AI avatars and translation or dubbing options.

The tool fits creators who care about narration quality, such as people making explainers, language content or short social videos for platforms like YouTube, Instagram and TikTok. You can edit scenes and text in the browser, and there is an iOS app as well. A free tier has been available without a credit card, while paid plans add commercial rights and more usage. Features and limits change, so check the official site for current plans.
use_steps: Sign up and paste a script, idea or blog URL.
Pick a voice, language and visual style.
Edit scenes, text and subtitles in the editor.
Export the video or publish it to social platforms.
pros: Large choice of AI voices and languages
cons: Commercial use depends on the paid plan
Generated visuals may need manual swapping
pricing_details: Fliki has offered a free tier with no credit card, plus paid plans that include commercial rights and higher usage. Plan details change, so check the official website for current plans.

faq.a: Fliki is an AI video and voice tool that turns text, scripts and articles into narrated videos.
Fliki has offered a free tier, with paid plans for commercial rights and more usage. Check the official site for what is included now.

faq.a: Treat outputs as a first draft. Review the video, voice and on-screen text yourself, confirm you have the rights to any uploaded material, and check licensing and privacy terms on the official website.

name: D-ID
tagline: Creative Reality Studio for making talking-avatar videos from photos and text.
best_for: Talking presenter videos from a photo or preset avatar
description:
D-ID offers Creative Reality Studio, a self-service platform for making videos with animated talking avatars. You can start from preset avatars, an uploaded photo or an image generated from text, then supply a script and let the tool produce lip-synced speech.

It supports many languages, voice cloning, AI script writing and a video translation feature that keeps lip sync across languages. Businesses use this style of tool for training, onboarding and marketing clips, and individuals use it for simple presenter videos. Some editing features, such as layers and expressions, have been limited in the mobile app. Credits generally cover a short length of video each. Plans change, so check the official site for current plans.
use_steps: Open the studio and pick a preset avatar or upload a photo.
Type or generate a script and choose a voice and language.
Adjust layers or expressions where available.
Generate the video and download it.
cons: Credit-based usage can run out quickly
Some editing features are limited on mobile
use_cases: Translating a video into other languages
pricing_details: D-ID has listed a trial plus paid tiers such as Lite, Pro and Advanced, and an Enterprise option, with credits covering short video lengths. Check the official website for current plans.

faq.a: D-ID provides Creative Reality Studio, a platform for creating videos with talking AI avatars from photos or presets.
D-ID has offered a trial with paid plans after it. Confirm current terms on the official site.

faq.a: Treat outputs as a first draft. Review the video, voice and on-screen text yourself, confirm you have the rights to any uploaded material, and check licensing and privacy terms on the official website.
